title: tcspecial configuration
description: The shape of a configuration: which sections there are, what an entry may say, and which words are words. Not whether it can be flown -- which attributes a node of a given type must state, whether two payloads claim one socket, whether a mean's inputs are the ones its links bind are rules about meaning, tested against real buses, and tcsverify is the one place they live. A file this accepts may still be refused, and the refusal will say why.

linkEntry.description: One line out of a node: the node it goes to, and which of that node's inputs it feeds where it feeds a named one. One entry per line, so several lines are several entries and nothing pairs by position.

target.description: The node this line goes to.

input.description: Which of that node's inputs the line feeds, or which of its data sinks it arrives at, where either has to be said.

include.description: Other files this one is made of, by name without an extension: named rather than discovered, so the set of files a configuration is made of is itself written down.

tcspecial.description: What tcspecial itself is configured with: where commands are taken, where beacons go, where the telemetry log is written. Everything optional here, because the editor has to be able to write a section somebody is halfway through filling in; what must be answered before a configuration flies is tcsverify's to say.

gateway.description: What the vehicle answers to: radio, the ground over UDP; fprime, an F´ flight computer's bridge component, over the same. cfs is specified in the design and not yet built, and is refused. Required, with no default.

interface.description: The interface the configuration was written for: the digest of the tcslibgs/xtce/link.xml its commands are laid out by, as 32 lower-case hex digits, which `tcsverify --interface-digest` prints. Required, and refused unless it is the build's own.

recv.description: Where tcspecial receives commands about the spacecraft and sends its responses.

send.description: Where the MOC sends them from and receives the responses.

source_base.description: The MOC's end, counted on by the payload's id.

dest_base.description: tcspecial's end, counted on by the payload's id.

source_base.description: Where a payload's telemetry leaves tcspecial, counted on by its id.

dest_base.description: Where it arrives at the ground, counted on by its id.

default_interval.description: How often a beacon is sent once the MOC has been heard from, as a length of time: 5 s, 500 ms. It was interval, and before that interval_ms, a bare number of milliseconds.

reset_interval.description: How often a beacon is sent across a restart, as a length of time: from a restart's being initiated, and from every start until the MOC is heard from. Not nought, and no longer than interval.

send.description: The socket tcspecial sends beacons from.

recv.description: The socket tcsmoc receives them on.

state_file.description: The file tcspecial keeps what must survive a restart in: whether the next start is commanded. On storage that survives a power cycle.

restart_arm_valid.description: How long a RESTART_ARM licenses a RESTART for, as a length of time: 20 min, 90 s. Twenty minutes where it is not stated; nought is refused.

payload_groups.description: Sets of payloads read on one interval, so that readings which will be compared are taken as close to together as the hardware allows.

interval.description: A number, whitespace, and a unit: 500 ms, 3 s, 1.5 s, 15 min, 6 h, 1 w. The whitespace is required and one or more characters of it will do, so 500 ms and 500  ms are the same and 500ms is refused. The units are us, ms, s, min, h, d and w, each a word of its own. Minutes are min and never m, a single m being one letter from ms and a thousand-fold apart from it; a month and a year are not units here. The number is decimal, whole or a fraction, with underscores allowed among the digits, so 1_000 ms, 1.5 s and 1500 ms are one interval written three ways. There is no hexadecimal and none is planned.

gateway.description: The ground links: what the editor's gateway working pane holds.

name.description: What this node is called, unique across the configuration.

type.description: What it is: the configuration's own word for the type. A link to the ground over the radio is gateway_radio; one to an F´ bridge component is gateway_fprime.

group.description: The payload group that reads it, where it is in one. Optional, though a payload that states a trigger needs one: the interval of its group is how often it is asked.

payload-out.description: The lines that leave this node by its `payload-out`, one entry each. An entry names the node the line goes to as its `target`, and `input` where it feeds a named input of that node. The short spellings are read too: the destination as a string, `node` or `node.terminal`, alone or in a list.

oneOf.description: One line, written as an entry.
One line, written as the node it reaches: `node` or `node.terminal`.
Several lines, each an entry or a destination.

gateway-out.description: The lines that leave this node by its `gateway-out`, one entry each. An entry names the node the line goes to as its `target`, and `input` where it feeds a named input of that node. The short spellings are read too: the destination as a string, `node` or `node.terminal`, alone or in a list.

oneOf.description: One line, written as an entry.
One line, written as the node it reaches: `node` or `node.terminal`.
Several lines, each an entry or a destination.

payload-in.description: Whether a line arrives at this node's `payload-in` sink. A record of the links written on the nodes they leave, and not a link: which node a line comes from is written on that node. A file may leave it out; one that disagrees with the links is refused where it is read.

gateway-in.description: Whether a line arrives at this node's `gateway-in` sink. A record of the links written on the nodes they leave, and not a link: which node a line comes from is written on that node. A file may leave it out; one that disagrees with the links is refused where it is read.

ground_base.description: Where the ground station is, as address:port. What each node linked into this gateway node produces is sent to that address, at that port plus the node's device id.

bridge_base.description: Where the F´ bridge component is, as address:port: a gateway_fprime node's ground_base. What each node linked into it produces is sent to that address, at that port plus the node's device id.

fprime_id_base.description: The first of the F´ IDs the bridge gives what arrives at a gateway_fprime node: each node linked into it is this ID plus its own device id. Decimal, or hexadecimal with 0x.

ip_protocol.description: The IP protocol number a node reached with `protocol: raw` reads and writes, 1 to 254. For a raw socket and nothing else.

sends_from.description: Where a datagram payload that speaks first sends from -- a host and a port over udp, as 10.0.0.7:7001, or a path over unix_dgram -- and so the one address it is read from: anything else that reaches the vehicle's socket is turned away and counted. Optional; without it the payload is learnt from the first datagram that arrives. Not on a payload that is asked or only driven, which is reached at its address.

stand_in.description: Where an hdlc, spi, rpmsg or iio payload is reached over UDP when it is simulated, as a loopback address and port: 127.0.0.1:7950. Used under --simulate=some or all, and not under none, the flight setting, when the device is opened.

trigger_interval.description: How often the trigger goes out, as a length of time: how often this payload is asked. For a payload that states a trigger and is in no group -- a payload in one is asked when its group is read. A payload with no trigger has nothing to send, and states `poll_interval` instead.

poll_interval.description: The least time between issuing one read of this node and issuing the next, as a length of time: a floor on the reading of a part nothing asks, not a cadence -- there is no telling how soon a descriptor will have anything, and what the interval prevents is reading again immediately for an answer already given. For a node in no group, and never beside a `trigger` -- a node that is asked is read because it was asked, which is `trigger_interval`.

read_delay.description: How long to wait between sending the trigger and reading the answer, as a length of time: what the part's interface document says it takes to answer. With one, a pass asks, waits and reads the answer to the question it just asked; with none, a pass reads what the last ask produced and asks again, so the reading is one interval old. Only beside a `trigger`.

init.description: What to write to this payload as the vehicle opens it -- at startup, and whenever the ground starts it again -- written as a trigger is: parts one after another, each a C string in quotes or bytes in hexadecimal in square brackets: '"READ\r"', '[55]', '"AT" [0D 0A]'. A write that fails stops the node from starting. Not on lines that are watched, a sensor's sample buffer, or a datagram payload that speaks first.

trigger.description: What to write to make this payload answer: parts one after another, each a C string in quotes or bytes in hexadecimal in square brackets: '"READ\r"', '[55]', '"AT" [0D 0A]'. A payload that states one is asked and is read at the interval of the payload group it is in; one that states none is only read, and a line delivering into it is refused. A payload says what asks it or that it sends on its own, never both, and there is no mode attribute: which it is follows from whether it has a trigger.

terminators.description: The byte sequences that each end a packet of a stream -- a line, or a tcp or unix_stream socket -- where the first of them arrives whole, which is the packet's last bytes. A list, one entry per terminator, each written as a trigger is: parts one after another, each a C string in quotes or bytes in hexadecimal in square brackets: '"READ\r"', '[55]', '"AT" [0D 0A]'. Not beside a length_prefix.

length_prefix.description: What a packet's first bytes say its length is, counting the bytes after them: u8, or u16be or u16le for two bytes with the more or the less significant first. The packet is delivered prefix and all. Needs a read_timeout, which may be none, and is not beside terminators.

state_interval.description: How often to report what a set of discrete lines is, as a length of time: 5 s. Events say when a line changed and this says what the lines are, so a payload may ask for either or both. It exists for the two things edges cannot do: a line that has not changed since the vehicle started tells the ground nothing, and the kernel's event queue is finite, so a burst can leave the ground holding a value that is wrong. Inputs only.

executable.description: The program this node runs: an app node's application, or the program a `process` computation runs on what arrives. Executed with a leading `~` and `$HOME` expanded as a shell would expand them -- to the home directory and to the value of the environment variable HOME, of whatever runs it. An app node's is run with the node's name as its first argument.

from.description: The gateway link it arrives on.

tcsgui.description: What the editor arranged: where each node was drawn. Last in the file and in a section of its own, because the sections above say what the vehicle carries and this says where somebody put the boxes on a screen. The flight software ignores it.
